characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy controls the scope and credibility of demonstrator work in phases two and three. It determines whether the project builds a single, focused FIDO2 demonstrator on mainstream Android, dual demonstrators spanning GrapheneOS and browser-based fallback, or includes speculative blockchain/DID approaches. Success is measured by producing non-production evidence that secure, standards-based fallback authentication is technically viable without exclusive Apple/Google reliance. The strategy directly impacts policy traction and procurement credibility.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Technical Feasibility Strategy strongly amplifies Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy. Credible demonstrators provide concrete evidence that platform-neutral access is feasible, raising policy proposals from abstract ideology to defensible technical reality. This evidence directly strengthens procurement negotiations by enabling authorities to specify platform-neutral requirements with confidence in vendor deliverability and architectural soundness.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Technical Feasibility Strategy conflicts with timeline and resource constraints implicit in Coalition Building Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy. Expanding demonstrator scope (blockchain/DIDs) risks delaying phase-two deliverables, weakening coalition momentum and EU visibility during critical procurement windows. Narrow focus on FIDO2 reduces technical breadth, potentially limiting coalition appeal to academic and innovation-oriented stakeholders seeking exploratory work.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy frames the platform-dependency problem for government and institutional decision-makers. It determines whether advocacy emphasizes continuity-of-service and supplier-concentration risks, or balances those arguments with privacy and democratic accountability. Success is measured by formal written responses from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, inclusion of platform-neutrality language in AltID procurement, and demonstrable influence over digital-identity policy decisions in phase three.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy is mutually reinforcing with Coalition Building Strategy and Technical Feasibility Strategy. A broad coalition spanning security experts, civil society, and academics strengthens policy advocacy reach and credibility. Credible demonstrators provide technical evidence that validates policy arguments, making resilience and continuity framing more persuasive to procurement and regulatory audiences.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy trades off breadth against clarity. Balancing continuity, privacy, and governance arguments risks diffusing message focus and attracting coalition partners with conflicting priorities, creating internal friction during critical procurement negotiations. Alternatively, narrow continuity-only framing alienates privacy advocates and civil society, reducing coalition size and external pressure needed to overcome institutional inertia.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy determines the scale, diversity, and political reach of the project's advocacy apparatus. It controls whether the coalition remains narrow (security and contingency experts), expands broadly (civil society, privacy, academia), or recruits internal dissenters from MitID and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. Success is measured by documented stakeholder engagement, coalition stability through procurement cycles, and demonstrated political pressure in phase three.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Coalition Building Strategy powerfully enables Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy. A broad coalition spanning civil-society, academia, and security expertise amplifies advocacy visibility and creates sustained political pressure on procurement decision-makers. Internal dissent from authorities signals legitimacy and creates window space for platform-neutral requirements to be formally considered rather than dismissed as external interference.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Coalition Building Strategy creates inherent tension with Procurement Influence Strategy focus and message coherence. Recruiting MitID insiders and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen dissenters risks creating competing factions with divergent strategic goals, weakening unified advocacy during procurement windows. Broad coalition inclusion (civil society, academia) may introduce mission drift or conflicting priority discussions that slow decision-making and reduce strategic agility.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy targets AltID and related digital-identity procurement cycles to embed platform-neutrality and fallback-authentication requirements into formal specifications and evaluation criteria. It determines whether the project advocates for general supplier-concentration language, specific technical requirements, or procurement scoring mechanisms rewarding platform-neutral design. Success is measured by inclusion of platform-neutral language in official AltID documents and demonstrable procurement leverage by month 24.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy depends directly on Technical Feasibility Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy. Credible demonstrators make platform-neutral requirements technically defensible in procurement documents. Clear policy advocacy reframes platform neutrality as a resilience and continuity imperative, not ideology, improving procurement receptivity. Coalition political pressure creates institutional space for procurement officers to justify neutrality language to existing operators.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Procurement Influence Strategy conflicts with EU Standards Engagement Strategy on resource allocation and timeline. Heavy investment in Danish AltID influence during phase three may starve EU-level standards engagement, reducing broader European legitimacy. Conversely, EU focus risks diverting coalition energy from Danish procurement windows, delaying AltID influence when institutional attention is highest and formal decisions are imminent.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy positions Denmark's platform-neutrality and fallback-authentication agenda within European Digital Identity Wallet governance and eIDAS2 technical working groups. It determines whether the project monitors EU processes passively, actively advocates for platform-neutral requirements, or champions exploratory frameworks like a 'sovereign identity sandbox.' Success is measured by documented input to EU bodies, alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet materials, and contributing language supporting platform-neutral or certified fallback mechanisms.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy amplifies Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy at the European level. EU-level standards pressure and alignment language create legitimacy for Danish platform-neutrality requirements, positioning them as aligned with broader European digital-sovereignty goals rather than isolated national interests. This reduces institutional resistance from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen and incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy directly competes with Procurement Influence Strategy for project resources and coalition attention during phase three. Scaling EU engagement requires sustained European stakeholder relationship-building, potentially diluting focus on time-sensitive Danish AltID procurement windows. Platform vendors also influence EU standards bodies; heavy EU advocacy may provoke counter-lobbying that delays both European and Danish progress simultaneously.
